newsitem.title: FRANCE: Franco-Spanish group near to Chile submarine sale.
newsitem.headline: Franco-Spanish group near to Chile submarine sale.

text.p: French Defence Minister Charles Millon said in an interview published on Thursday that Paris and Madrid were close to signing a contract for the sale of two Scorpene-type submarines to Chile.
Aides told reporters the deal would be worth 2.5 billion francs ($455 million).

"I have high hopes that that we can engage in real cooperation concerning submarines with Chile which has selected the Scorpene produced by DCN-Cherbourg and offered by the Franco-Spanish DCNI-Bazan consortium," Millon told the business daily Les Echos.
"There is still some work to be done before the contract is concluded but I hope that will happen soon," he said.
The French and Spanish state firms working on the submarine are Direction des Constructions Navales of France and Empresa Nacional Bazan of Spain.

Scorpene-type submarines, designed to attack submarines and surface vessels, have six torpedo tubes. They are conventionally propelled, have a crew of up to 37 and can stay at sea for 50 days without being resupplied. ($1=5.526 French Franc)
